item.title: Marcus Smart's Stunning Lakers Revival Rewrites 2026 Playoffs
item.description:
Nine games in street clothes. Nine games of doubt. Then Marcus Smart walked into Game 2 and shredded the Houston Rockets for 25 points, five threes, seven assists, and five steals.

If you thought the Lakers’ 2026 playoff run would hinge on LeBron James and Deandre Ayton alone, Smart just changed your mind.

Quick Summary: Marcus Smart signed a two-year, $11 million deal with the Lakers in July 2025. After battling injuries that cost him nine late-season games, he erupted in Game 2 of the first round, leading Los Angeles to a 101-94 win and a 2-0 series lead over Houston.

item.title: Cameron Johnson's Surprising Rise Is Fueling the Nuggets' Playoff Push
item.description:
With about a month left in the NBA regular season, Cameron Johnson is finally starting to look like the player the Denver Nuggets envisioned when they acquired him. After battling injuries, adjusting to a new system, and admitting there is “still an element of figuring it out,” the veteran forward is stringing together his best stretch of basketball – and the timing could not be more important.

Quick Summary

  • Cameron Johnson has scored at least 15 points in three consecutive games, only the second time he has done that this season
  • He recently put up 18 points, 4 rebounds, 3 assists, a steal, and a block against the Lakers
  • Johnson has dealt with back spasms and an ankle injury, limiting his minutes in recent games
  • He is entering the final year of a $23.1 million contract and becomes extension-eligible this summer
  • The Denver Post called the Nuggets an “NBA Finals contender” when Johnson and Christian Braun find their groove

Cameron Johnson Admits He Is Still Adjusting to Denver

Honesty is refreshing in professional sports, and Johnson has been remarkably candid about his transition. Speaking to Bennett Durando of the Denver Post, the forward acknowledged that his first season with the Nuggets has required significant adjustment.

item.title: Derrick Jones Jr.'s Essential Role in the Clippers' 2026 Playoff Push
item.description:
A player once known primarily for slam dunk contests is quietly producing top-20 fantasy value and anchoring the Clippers’ defense during their playoff chase.

Quick Summary: Derrick Jones Jr. has emerged as the LA Clippers’ X-factor in their 2026 playoff push. He’s scored in double digits in 8 of his last 9 games, recorded 15 combined steals and blocks in 3 games, and has been described as delivering “elite two-way production.” However, recent injuries — including a head injury against the Knicks and a knee collision — have raised concerns about his availability down the stretch.

item.title: Kawhi Leonard Fuels Clippers' Stunning Turnaround After Disastrous Start
item.description:
Few players in NBA history have carried a team from the edge of irrelevance back into the playoff picture the way Kawhi Leonard is doing right now. After the LA Clippers lost 21 of their first 27 games this season, most analysts had already written their obituary. Leonard had other plans.

Key Takeaways

  • Kawhi Leonard is averaging 28.0 points, 6.4 rebounds, 3.7 assists, and 2.0 steals per game on elite shooting splits
  • The Clippers clawed back from a 6-21 start to reach .500 at 32-32, surpassing the Warriors for 8th in the Western Conference
  • An NBA investigation into a $28 million endorsement deal with Aspiration has raised salary cap circumvention questions
  • Despite the turnaround, Leonard insists there is “nothing to be happy about” — the job is far from finished

Kawhi Leonard’s Monster Season by the Numbers

Leonard’s individual performance this season has been nothing short of extraordinary. At 34 years old, the two-time Finals MVP is putting up numbers that rival his peak seasons in San Antonio and Toronto.
